chapters.title: Why you're still in it
chapters.teaser: The real reason your soul keeps saying 'let's see where it goes'.

chapters.title: What you actually want
chapters.teaser: Not what sounds chill. What you'd ask for if you weren't worried.

chapters.title: How you read mixed signals
chapters.teaser: Your decoding habit, and a better way to get information.

chapters.title: The talk, your way
chapters.teaser: How to ask 'what are we' in words that fit your soul.

chapters.title: Your line
chapters.teaser: The one thing you shouldn't keep accepting.

chapters.title: Either way, you're okay
chapters.teaser: What comes next, whatever answer you get.

text.why-you-stay: Im Water is the ocean, and you love your freedom. Honestly, a situationship can suit you for a while. No pressure, plenty of space, nobody asking where you are on a Saturday. You might stay because it's easy, or because defining it would feel like signing up for a cage. But check yourself here. Are you genuinely happy with how undefined it is, or are you avoiding the question because answering it would mean staying in one harbor for longer than you're used to? Both answers are allowed. Just make sure it's the real one.
text.what-you-want: You might want something deeper than you're admitting. Im Water often thinks it wants freedom, when what it really wants is freedom with someone. What would good commitment look like for you, in your own terms? Space to roam, with a home to come back to? Separate adventures and shared Sundays? Define your version without borrowing anyone else's template. It doesn't have to look like your friends' relationships or anything on a screen. It only has to fit you and one other person. Write it as three short lines. If you can't, that's a sign to sit with the question a little longer before you ask them anything.
text.mixed-signals: Here's the twist: you might be the one sending mixed signals. Im Water flows, warm and present one week, distant and busy the next, and doesn't always notice the change from the outside. And when they're unclear, you tend to drift rather than ask. Check both sides of this honestly. What am I communicating with my behavior, and what am I avoiding asking with my words? Sometimes the fog you're trying to see through is partly your own weather. A simple fix: tell them when you're going quiet for a few days. It costs one message and saves a lot of guessing.
text.the-talk: Your version of the talk can be relaxed and open, which suits you. Maybe on a walk or a long drive, where nobody has to stare across a table. The risk is keeping it so light that nothing actually gets decided. Say what you want, even if it's a bit unconventional: I like this, I want to keep seeing you, and I want to know if it's just us. Be specific about the parts that matter. Freedom works much better with clear terms than with vague vibes. And listen to their answer as carefully as you'd study a map before a big trip.
text.your-line: Your hard line is control. Im Water won't stay anywhere it's boxed in or monitored. But notice your other line too, the one you talk about less: being someone's option. Even an ocean wants to matter to the shore. Decide what you need on both sides, room to breathe and real importance. When those aren't there, let the tide carry you somewhere else, honestly and with a clear goodbye, rather than simply drifting out of contact and hoping they get the message. Both lines can exist at once. Wanting space and wanting to matter isn't a contradiction. It's just being honest.
text.either-way: However it lands, you'll flow on. If they want more, great, build a version with room to breathe for both of you. If not, you'll explore, travel, meet people and recover quickly. Just make sure you actually feel it before you set sail again. Oceans have real depths, and you're allowed to visit yours. Give the feeling one honest evening of your attention. Then go wherever you want to go, lighter, and a little clearer about what you're looking for next time. Maybe write it down somewhere you'll find it again on your next trip.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You love your freedom, Im. That's real.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also love not answering hard questions. Also real.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Maybe you want freedom with someone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Warm one week, gone the next. You might be the mixed signal.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Define your own version of commitment.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Freedom with terms. Write them down. On land.

spring.intro: Spring Im is a river feeding everything along its banks. Wood was in command when you were born and Water nourishes Wood, so you give energy freely: ideas, adventures, encouragement. In a situationship you probably make it exciting. Spontaneous trips, late calls, big plans for later. You might also be the one keeping it undefined, because freedom feels like oxygen. Spring Im's question is whether the vagueness serves you or just keeps options open out of habit. If you want it to grow, flowing in every direction won't do it. Pick a channel. Even rivers choose a path to the sea.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You love freedom so much a situationship became your whole lifestyle, Im.

summer.intro: Summer Im runs warm and restless. You were born while Fire was in charge, and Water controls Fire, so you're used to managing heat: excitement, chaos, other people's moods. In a situationship you might be the one keeping everything breezy. You cool down any intensity, change the subject when it gets serious, keep the fun going. It works until you notice you're managing them instead of being with them. Summer Im's honest move is to stop steering for a moment. Let a serious conversation happen without rescuing it with a joke. See what they say when the water is still.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to cool every serious moment with a joke, Im.

autumn.intro: Autumn Im springs clear and cold from stone. Metal was in command when you were born and generates Water, so your chart is strong: confident, deep, self-sufficient. In a situationship that self-sufficiency can be the issue. You don't need them, so you never ask. You enjoy the connection, then vanish into your own plans for a week. They might read that as low interest. Strong autumn Im's blind spot is assuming everyone can handle your tides. If you want this to be something, show up consistently for a while. If you don't, say so kindly. Either is fairer than drifting.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Vanishing for a week then sending a meme is not a communication strategy, Im.

winter.intro: Winter Im is the deep sea at its fullest. Water held your season and doubled your element, so you feel enormously and show very little. In a situationship you might be secretly invested and outwardly breezy, a calm surface hiding strong currents. You can keep this up for months. The winter blind spot is that nobody can navigate water they can't see. They may be guessing, just like you. Winter Im needs a shoreline: a clear moment where you say what you feel and ask what they want. It doesn't have to be dramatic. Just real enough to break the surface.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They can't read currents they can't see, Im. Show a little.

earth.intro: Im, you met walls early: you were born in the Earth days. Earth controls Water, so you're used to pushing against limits and flowing around them. A situationship can feel perfect at first because there are no banks at all. Then the lack of shape starts to bother you, and you drift off to see if anyone follows. That's a test the other person doesn't know they're taking. The talk for you is about structure, not feelings first: how often, how serious, how exclusive. Banks make rivers go somewhere.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Disappearing to see if they notice is a quiz they never signed up for, Im.

strength.strong: Your chart pours plenty into your water, Im, so you're free, confident and hard to pin down. A strong Im is often the slippery one: keen one week, distant the next, always with a good reason. The blind spot of a strong current is assuming the other person can keep up or doesn't mind. They might mind a lot and not say. If you want this, slow down and be consistent. If you don't, say so. Your freedom matters, and so does their clarity.
strength.weak: With little support in your chart, Im, your water takes the shape of whoever's nearby. Here you might be flowing around their schedule, their moods, their indecision, and losing your own direction. The blind spot is following their current so long you forget yours. Pick one thing you'd like from them and say it. Give yourself a quiet, private check-in point to decide whether this is moving or circling. Banks help a river reach somewhere instead of spreading thin.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practice clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyze every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you've planned your future together. They haven't planned Saturday.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: That growing energy is lovely. Point it at what you want, not only at them.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: one great date and you're naming the dog. Breathe.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is magnetic. Let them match it before you double it.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: you've waited so patiently you've basically become their furniture.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness is a gift. It's fair to ask for steadiness back.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal: you've drafted an ultimatum. Maybe try a question first.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is strength. Soften the delivery and it lands beautifully.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you analyzed one 'haha' with three friends and a tarot app.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your sensitivity notices so much. Check the signals against actual actions too.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood can make it hard to picture what you want. Try imagining it.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no vision. You're seeing where it goes without looking anywhere.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can make it hard to show interest. A little warmth helps.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. They genuinely cannot tell if you like them. Neither can I.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it easy to drift. Choose one thing you're sure about.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth, no ground. You change your mind about them every other day.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal can blur your line. You can decide what you won't accept.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal means no line. You'll accept 'wyd' at midnight forever.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can make feelings hard to say. Try writing them first.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. You'd rather move countries than say 'I like you.'

gap-wood.title: The calendar invite and the riverbank
gap-wood.text: A Gap Wood is the kind of person who can turn your best 2 a.m. idea into an actual plan by Friday. You love that. You also feel it when the plans start to close in. Gap suggests the weekend, then the next weekend, then meeting their parents in the spring, and somewhere in there you start answering with 'let's see'. You don't mean no. You mean don't fence me in. Gap tends to hear the 'let's see' and tighten the plan, which makes you go vaguer, which makes them tighten more. That loop is the whole situationship. Your texting adds fuel. You vanish for a day because you were deep in something, then send a brilliant midnight essay. Gap reads the silence first and the essay second. Your signal is freedom, and to a tree it can look like you're keeping options open. For the talk, give Gap the commitment part in plain words, and then the freedom part: I want this to be a relationship. I also need room to wander off into my own head sometimes. Can we have both? Offer one small anchor yourself, before Gap asks. That's the gesture that shows you're choosing the riverbank.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, your midnight essays are gorgeous. A two-word check-in matters too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gap's calendar invite is not a love letter.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Name the loop and it loses half its grip.

eul-wood.title: Fast growth, no map
eul-wood.text: An Eul Wood grows toward you without being asked. You mention a festival, Eul has the tickets. You go on about a new obsession, Eul is suddenly into it too. It's flattering and easy, and with you, Eul is playful in a way that keeps everything moving. The drift starts with your current. You dive into a project or a trip and go silent for a day, then come back with forty memes at 2 a.m. To you, that's normal tide. To Eul, the silence can feel quietly lonely, and Eul tends not to say so. Eul adapts instead, so you might never notice anything was wrong. Both of you like freedom, which means the 'what are we' conversation gets postponed politely and indefinitely. Your signal is freedom, and to someone who bends toward you, it can look like you're not holding any of the weight. For the talk, don't wait for Eul to raise it. Pushing isn't Eul's style. Say: I like what we have and I'd like to call it something. I'll still wander off sometimes. Will you tell me when that feels lonely? A two-word check-in from you does more than any midnight essay.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: River and vine. Fast growth, lots of fun, no map.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, a two-word check-in. You can manage two words.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul is allowed to ask instead of overthinking.

byeong-fire.title: Who sets first over the ocean
byeong-fire.text: A Byeong Fire is the sun over your ocean, magnificent and very, very warm. They throw themselves at life and at you with an enthusiasm that's flattering and sometimes a lot. You like their light. You also need your depth, and depth requires some silence. The drift here is that your silence gets loud. You go quiet for a day to think, recharge, or follow an idea into a rabbit hole. Byeong sends three messages, a voice note and a 'helloooo'. You feel flooded and go a bit cooler. Byeong reads the coolness as rejection and pushes harder. You both end up confirming each other's worst read: you think Byeong is too much, Byeong thinks you're not interested. Your moods can also dampen Byeong's joy without you meaning to. Your signal is space, which a sun reads as clouds. For the talk, give Byeong something warm and specific, because warmth is Byeong's language: I'm not ignoring you when I go quiet. I'm thinking. And I do want us to be together. Can we figure out a rhythm? Then offer a small promise yourself, like one message a day, even if it's a dot. Suns can live with clouds. They struggle with nothing at all.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong reads silence as trouble. It's just Im thinking.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, one daily ping. A dot counts. Send the dot.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ocean and sun. Magnificent, once you agree on the tides.

jeong-fire.title: A lantern on the river at midnight
jeong-fire.text: 丁壬 is one of the classic heavenly combinations, and with a Jeong Fire, you understand why. Jeong listens to your midnight theories like they matter. They write you thoughtful messages that you actually reread. With Jeong, your restless mind feels at home. The drift here is your tide. You go quiet for a day or two, lost in a project or a plan, and come back with a three-paragraph essay. For you, that's normal. For Jeong, the silence before it can feel like you're slipping away. Jeong might reach out more, ask where you've been, want reassurance. You can feel that as a fence and drift further. Jeong's flame flickers with anxiety, your waters get choppier, and the cycle runs on. Your signal is freedom, and to someone who loves this focused, it can look like you're always half-gone. For the talk, name the cycle; it loses half its power when you do. Then say it clearly: I want to be with you. When I go quiet, it's not about you. Can we make it a proper relationship? And check in, even when you're lost in thought. One line is enough. The lantern needs to see the river is still there.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: 丁壬, a lantern on the river. Deep, easy, rare.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, check in when you vanish into your head. One line.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong can trust the rhythm and still ask for what Jeong needs.

mu-earth.title: The dam, the river and the booked table
mu-earth.text: A Mu Earth is the dam to your river: steady, solid and quietly immovable. You love how calm they are. You also find yourself wanting to shake things up every time you're with them. The same restaurant, the same Thursday, a plan made three weeks ahead. The drift here is control versus flow. Mu likes things held in place. You like to decide on the day. When Mu books a table for next Friday, you might feel boxed in and change it, and Mu gets frustrated. You find the routine boring; Mu finds your changes unreliable. Money's a flashpoint too: Mu saves, you spend on experiences. The 'what are we' question sits under all of it, unasked, because asking feels like signing up for more structure. Your signal is spontaneity, which a mountain can read as not taking this seriously. For the talk, send something steady first. Keep a plan you made. Turn up on time. Then say: I know I'm all over the place. But I want to be with you. Can we work out how much structure we each need? And let Mu keep a few plans without you rewriting them.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The dam and the river. Strong on both sides.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, keep one plan exactly as made. Just one.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu could allow a little irregularity. The river needs to move.

gi-earth.title: The pigeon meme and 'are we still on?'
gi-earth.text: A Gi Earth is a garden that welcomes you even when you arrive like a storm. They're caring, steady and attentive, and they make your chaotic life feel a bit more held. You love that. You also feel it when the holding starts to feel like managing. The drift here is your rhythm. You send bursts, then go quiet. You change plans on the day. Gi asks practical questions, are we still on, what time, should I book, and you reply with a meme about a pigeon. Gi worries about where this is going. You wave it off as overthinking. Gi tries to make things more predictable, more check-ins, more plans, and you feel restless and drift further. Gi can end up exhausted and you can end up feeling hemmed in, and nobody has said what this is. Your signal is spontaneity, which can feel to Gi like instability. For the talk, give Gi something steady to stand on: I want us to be a couple. I'm messy with plans, but I'm not messy about you. Then commit to one thing: a message a day. Answer the practical question first. Send the pigeon after.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The garden and the flood. Care meets chaos.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, answer 'are we still on?' before the pigeon meme.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi gets one message a day, then stops counting. That's the deal.

gyeong-metal.title: Excellent teammates, lonely lovers
gyeong-metal.text: A Gyeong Metal is the clear blade cutting through your fog. You like how decisive they are. You like that they don't play games. With Gyeong, you never wonder what they think about a restaurant, a film or your terrible flat. You're less sure what they think about you. The drift here is the gap between practical partnership and emotional closeness. You two do things brilliantly together: trips, projects, a whole furniture-assembly afternoon without casualties. But neither of you does tenderness on purpose. You go quiet in bursts; Gyeong wants to know where you stand. Gyeong's bluntness can chill you, and you drift a little. Gyeong reads the drift as unreliability, and gets blunter. The 'what are we' talk keeps getting postponed, because you both treat it like a meeting no one wants to call. Your signal is flexibility, which steel can read as not being committed. For the talk, give Gyeong a direct answer, since that's what they respect most: I'd like to be with you. I need some freedom, but I'm not looking elsewhere. Can we call it what it is? Then agree on one minimum check-in. Keep it, even on your vanishing days.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Cold steel, deep water. Clear minds, strong currents.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Excellent teammates. Now try being lovers on purpose.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Commitment and freedom in the same sentence. You can.

sin-metal.title: A week of planning and a hoodie
sin-metal.text: A Sin Metal sparkles when it meets your water. They're sharp, elegant and funny, and they seem to like your chaos more than most people do. You make them freer. They make you feel noticed by someone with taste. It works. It also produces scenes like this one: Sin has been planning a dinner for a week, the restaurant, the table, the outfit. You turn up late, underdressed and very excited about a new idea. Sin is quiet for the rest of the evening. You have no idea why. That's the drift in this pair. Sin cares about details you don't notice, and when you miss them, Sin can feel neglected. When Sin comments, you feel critiqued. Your bursts and silences can leave Sin reading meaning into gaps. And the 'what are we' question gets lost under it all. Your signal is spontaneity, which can look careless to someone who puts this much care in. For the talk, notice the effort in Sin's messages and say so. Then: I don't always get the details right, but I'm serious about you. Shall we make this a relationship? And next time, ask what Sin has planned. Then turn up on time.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: A jewel washed in the river. Clarity and sparkle.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, the hoodie to the planned dinner? Bold.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin should name the details that matter. Im can't read them.

im-water.title: Japan has been 'next month' for a year
im-water.text: Two Im Waters in a situationship is two oceans meeting: vast, brilliant and very hard to hold. You understand each other's need for freedom without explanation. You can disappear for a week and come back with a three-paragraph thought, and the other one gets it. Your conversations are some of the best of your life. And still, nothing is anchored. The drift for two oceans is parallel lives. You're both having great adventures, just not together. Plans dissolve because nobody holds them: 'we should go to Japan', 'let's do that festival', 'next month for sure'. Both of you avoid being pinned down, so the 'what are we' question keeps getting dodged with a joke or a new topic. When both of you are low at the same time, the tide goes very far out, and nobody's on the shore. Your signal is freedom, and the other one reads it as freedom too, which feels perfect until one of you wants more and doesn't know how to say so. For the talk, choose an anchor, not a cage: I love our freedom. I also want us to be together. Can we be both? Then agree on one anchor message a week, and keep it.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Two oceans. Brilliant, vast, and very, very free.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Japan has been 'next month' for a year. Anchor something.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: One anchor message a week. Keep it.

gye-water.title: Talked over at the party, noticed by the rain
gye-water.text: A Gye Water is rain to your ocean: the same element, a completely different depth. With Gye, you feel understood in a quieter way. They notice what you don't say, and their messages are poetic in a way that slows you down. The drift in this situationship is size. You're big: big ideas, big plans, big presence. Gye is subtle, and Gye can feel overshadowed. In groups, you might talk over Gye without noticing, and Gye notices and quietly stores it away. Your restlessness can overwhelm Gye, and Gye's moods can pull your energy down. When either of you is uncomfortable, you both drift away instead of talking, you into a project, Gye into silence. Your bursts and Gye's absences can leave long gaps where nothing is said, and the question of what you are floats in them. Your signal is momentum, which can make a raindrop feel lost in the waves. For the talk, make it small and close: one-on-one, no groups, no big plans. I'd like you to be my person. Would you? And remember Gye's need for intimacy. A quiet evening for two can mean more to Gye than a whole adventure.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The ocean and the rain. Same water, different depths.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Im, you talked over Gye at the party. Gye noticed.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Silence isn't rejection. Say so, both of you.
